title: The messengers: one message, Adam to Muhammad ﷺ
hook: You didn't join a new religion. You joined the oldest message there is.

screens.text: People sometimes say Islam started in Arabia in the 600s. Muslims see it differently: the same message has come again and again since the first human. Today, meet the messengers, the fourth article of faith.
**One message, many messengers.** Allah sent a messenger to every nation [Q 16:36]. Each one brought the same core: worship Allah alone, because there is no other god [Q 21:25].
bubbles: The Qur'an names twenty-five of them, and says there were others it doesn't name [Q 4:163–165; Revealed Path ch. 11].
A **nabi** (prophet) receives revelation. A **rasul** (messenger) is also sent to deliver a message to a people.

screens.text: Tap through, from the first human to the last messenger.

events.title: Adam
events.text: The first human, and the first of the prophets.

events.title: Nuh (Noah)
events.text: Sent to his people with the same call as every messenger: worship Allah alone [Q 42:13].

events.title: Ibrahim (Abraham)
events.text: The Qur'an calls him a Muslim: someone who submits to God [Q 3:67].

events.title: Muhammad ﷺ
events.text: The seal of the prophets. No prophet comes after him [Q 33:40].

screens.prompt: Now from memory: put these prophets in order, first to last.
screens.feedback: From the first human to the last messenger. Same God, same core message, sent again and again.

screens.text: **What they had in common.** They were human: they ate food and walked in the markets [Q 25:20]. Each spoke his people's language [Q 14:4].
bubbles: They were truthful and trustworthy, protected from serious sin, and delivered the message in full [Revealed Path ch. 11].
After their names, Muslims say *'alayhis-salam* (peace be upon him).

screens.prompt: True or myth? Sort each one.

items.text: The messengers ate food and walked in the markets
items.why: True. They were human beings, not angels or gods [Q 25:20].

items.text: Each messenger spoke his own people's language
items.why: True. Each one was sent in the language of his people [Q 14:4].

items.text: Muslims believe in some prophets and reject others
items.why: Myth. Muslims love them all and believe in every one, without accepting some and rejecting others [Q 2:136].

items.text: Each messenger brought a different god to worship
items.why: Myth. Every one brought the same core: worship Allah alone [Q 21:25].

screens.prompt: Match each prophet to something the Qur'an says about him.

pairs.right: Neither Jew nor Christian, but a Muslim who submitted to God
Born to Maryam (Mary) without a father
Rose from prison and was reunited with his family

screens.text: **The last one.** Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets [Q 33:40]. He didn't bring a new religion: Allah says it's the same one He gave Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa [Q 42:13].
bubbles: The Qur'an even calls Ibrahim a Muslim, someone who submits to God [Q 3:67]. You joined his family.

screens.after: of the prophets: no prophet comes after him.

options.feedback: Yes. He's the seal of the prophets, the last one [Q 33:40].
Not quite. Adam was the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the seal, the last [Q 33:40].
Not quite. He didn't found a new religion; he brought the same one. He's the seal of the prophets [Q 42:13].

screens.character: Chris, a coworker. Grew up Baptist, friendly, likes history documentaries, a little skeptical.
screens.setup: On break, Chris says: "No offense, but isn't Islam kind of a newer religion that borrowed stories from the Bible?"
screens.goal: Explain in your own words that Muslims see Islam as the same message all the prophets brought, from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, and that Muslims love and believe in the prophets Chris knows.
screens.success_looks_like: The convert stays relaxed, names a few shared prophets (Abraham, Moses, Jesus), explains 'one God, one message, many messengers', mentions that Muhammad ﷺ is the last, and doesn't put down Chris's faith.
screens.coach_notes: Chris pushes once or twice: 'So you think Jesus was just a prophet?' and 'Why would God need another prophet?'. He's curious, never hostile. Debrief: praise a clear 'one message' line; if they got defensive or argued about the Bible, model a calmer version; remind them Day 27 covers Jesus and 'I'm still learning that' is fine.

chips: Who are the twenty-five prophets named in the Qur'an?
Is Jesus more than a prophet in Islam?
Were there prophets in Africa or the Americas?
Why is Muhammad ﷺ the last prophet?

screens.text: Notice two prophets in your prayers today.
steps: In the last sitting of each prayer, say the **Salat Ibrahimiyya** as usual
As you say it, remember you're asking blessings on Muhammad ﷺ and Ibrahim, and their families
screens.optional_extra: Tell one person the short version: "Same God, same message, from Adam to Muhammad."

You belong to a family of believers older than any nation.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- A messenger was sent to every nation [Q 16:36], all with the message that there is no god but Allah [Q 21:25]. Some are named and some are not [Q 4:163–165]; twenty-five are named in the Qur'an [Revealed Path ch. 11].
- Prophet (nabi) receives revelation; messenger (rasul) also has a mission to convey it [Revealed Path ch. 11].
- Messengers were human [Q 25:20], spoke their people's language [Q 14:4], were truthful, trustworthy, protected from sin and conveyed fully [Revealed Path ch. 11]. Believers make no distinction between them in belief [Q 2:136; Q 2:285].
- Muhammad ﷺ is the seal of the prophets [Q 33:40]. The same religion was ordained for Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad ﷺ [Q 42:13]. Ibrahim was "a Muslim," submitting to God [Q 3:67].
- Match facts: Musa spoken to directly [Q 4:164]; Dawud given the Zabur [Q 4:163]; Isa born of Maryam without a father [Q 3:45–47]; Yusuf reunited with his family [Q 12:100].

**Likely questions**
- *"Who are the twenty-five?"* Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Yusuf, Ayyub, Shu'ayb, Musa, Harun, Dhul-Kifl, Dawud, Sulayman, Ilyas, al-Yasa', Yunus, Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ [Revealed Path ch. 11]. Offer English names.
- *"Is Jesus more than a prophet?"* In Islam he's a mighty messenger and the Messiah, born miraculously, but not divine [Q 4:171]. Day 27 covers it. Be respectful of Christian belief.
- *"Prophets in Africa, the Americas?"* Every nation received a messenger [Q 16:36], and many aren't named [Q 4:164]. Don't name specific historical figures as prophets.
- *"Why is Muhammad ﷺ the last?"* The Qur'an says so [Q 33:40]; his message is for all people and the Qur'an is preserved (Day 37).
- *"What about stories where prophets did bad things?"* Muslims believe prophets were protected from serious sin [Revealed Path ch. 11]; the Qur'an's accounts differ from some other tellings. Don't debate other scriptures.
- *"How many prophets were there in total?"* Allah knows; the Qur'an names some and not others [Q 4:164]. Don't cite numbers from collections outside the bank.

**Escalate:** claims that someone after Muhammad ﷺ is a prophet (fixed sectarian policy, rule 11: calm mainstream answer, route to the imam).

**Don't**
- Don't belittle Christianity or Judaism (rule 8).
- Don't name anyone as a prophet beyond the Qur'an's named list.
- Don't describe or depict prophets' appearance (Spec §11).

**Role-play brief:** Chris is a friendly, curious ex-Baptist coworker who thinks Islam "borrowed" Bible stories. Pushes on Jesus being "just a prophet" and "why another prophet". Debrief: name a clear "one message" line, smooth any defensiveness, point to Day 27.
